description: Across the whole US market: the companies whose insiders bought (or sold) the most in the open market over a period, ranked by USD value. Each company has the total value, shares, number of filings and insiders, the share of the value that was under a Rule 10b5-1 plan, and its largest filing with source_url. Planned trades are left out by default (planned=exclude) and the answer says so. Common and other non-derivative shares only (Form 4 Table I). Default: the last 7 days; at most 90 days, and at most 31 for periods before 2026-07-01.

days.description: Look back this many days from today. Default 7. Leave out when you give from.

limit.description: How many companies to return. Default 10.

planned.description: Rule 10b5-1 trading plans: the Form 4 box says at least one transaction in the filing was made under a plan the insider set up in advance, so its timing was fixed earlier. The box is per filing: an open-market purchase or sale in such a filing carries planned_trade=true, another line (a gift, a conversion) planned_trade=null with a note. The filter works on the filing's box: exclude = leave out every line of a filing with the box ticked, only = only those lines, all = both. The checkbox exists on Form 4 since April 2023; older filings have planned_trade=null and count as not planned. Default exclude.

role.description: Only filings by a director, an officer, or an owner of more than 10% of the company.

side.description: buy = open-market purchases (default), sell = open-market sales.

name: top_insider_activity
title: Companies with the most insider buying or selling (SEC Form 4)
